faqs.a: You need a full-time job offer from a New Zealand employer accredited by Immigration New Zealand, in a role that has passed an approved Job Check. You also need at least two years of relevant work experience or a qualification at level 4 or higher, and English language evidence for skill level 3 to 5 roles.
faqs.q: What are the requirements for the Accredited Employer Work Visa?

faqs.a: Applying for the AEWV costs from NZ$1,540: a NZ$480 application fee plus a NZ$1,060 immigration levy. Extra costs can include medical examinations, police certificates, and English tests, which may add NZ$500 to NZ$1,000 depending on your circumstances. Budget early and keep receipts for every official charge, since hidden third-party fees are a common warning sign of migration scams.
faqs.q: How much does the New Zealand work visa cost in 2026?

faqs.a: The AEWV is granted for up to five years for most roles, though jobs at skill levels 4 and 5 are limited to three years. Residence pathways include the Skilled Migrant Category after two years and the Green List Tier 1 Straight to Residence route for highly skilled occupations.
faqs.q: How long does the AEWV last and does it lead to residency?

faqs.a: Since March 2026, the median wage no longer sets AEWV pay; jobs must pay at least the market rate for the role. The immigration median wage of NZ$35.00 an hour, set in March 2026, still determines whether you can bring a partner on a work visa and whether your job counts toward residence.

metaDescription: New Zealand work visa 2026: Accredited Employer Work Visa rules, NZ$1,540 cost, 5-year stays, NZ$35/hour median wage, skill levels and application process.

sections.content:
The Accredited Employer Work Visa is New Zealand's main temporary work visa and the route most skilled migrants apply through in 2026. It works in three stages: the employer gains accreditation from Immigration New Zealand, the employer gets an approved Job Check for the specific role, and then you apply for the visa with that job offer.

You need at least two years of relevant work experience or a qualification at level 4 or higher on the New Zealand Qualifications framework. The job must be at least 30 hours a week and pay at least the market rate for the role. For skill level 3 roles, English language evidence has been required since June 2026, while levels 4 and 5 already required it.
sections.title: The Accredited Employer Work Visa Explained

sections.content:
Applying for the AEWV costs from NZ$1,540, made up of a NZ$480 application fee and a NZ$1,060 immigration levy. Medical examinations, police certificates, and English tests can add several hundred dollars more. Immigration New Zealand currently decides about 80 percent of applications within five and a half weeks.

The visa is granted for up to five years for most roles, with jobs at skill levels 4 and 5 limited to three years. It is a pathway to residence: after two years in an eligible role you can move through the Skilled Migrant Category, while Green List Tier 1 occupations can go straight to residence. Since 24 August 2026, the Skilled Migrant route has three qualifying pathways covering points, skilled work experience, and trades.
sections.title: Costs, Processing and Residence Pathways

sections.content:
Since March 2025, employers no longer have to pay the median wage for AEWV roles; they must pay at least the minimum wage and the market rate, meaning what a New Zealander would earn in the same role and region. The immigration median wage of NZ$35.00 an hour, set in March 2026, still matters for partner visas and residence.

High-demand sectors in 2026 include healthcare, IT, construction, and engineering. Beware of scams: no legitimate employer asks you to pay for a job offer or a Job Check, and you cannot apply for the AEWV without an offer from an accredited employer. Always verify accreditation and the Job Check through Immigration New Zealand's official channels before committing money or resigning your current job.
